clue.text: Frenzied, eating doughnut or tropical root

indicators.note: one word eating another takes it into its middle, so the doughnut goes inside

parts.note: frenzied means manic
a doughnut is ring-shaped, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A list of options: something frenzied, a doughnut being eaten, or a root from the tropics.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc is another name for cassava, the starchy tuber grown across hot countries.

clue.text: Rely on school turning up 6 in 25

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the school's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone told they can count on a school reappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BILL and 25 is AMERICA: in the US a paper money note is called a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a piece of paper currency a bill, which Britons call a banknote.

clue.text: Secrets for cooking with raw salad ingredient

indicators.note: something put up for cooking gets mixed and transformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kitchen secrets for preparing a raw salad leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' shuffles SECRETS and RAW together.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercress is a peppery leafy plant commonly eaten in salads.

clue.text: Departed to the north along with others

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the departed are the late, so departed means late

explanation.surface: Someone left heading north with companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al. is the Latin abbreviation used in citations to mean 'and others'.

clue.text: Blimey! Arab in crumpled hat shows urge to fib

parts.note: 'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Blimey!'

indicators.note: the Arab sits in the crumpled hat, inside its letters
a crumpled hat is out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an Omani is an Arab from Oman

explanation.surface: An exclamation at an Arab in a battered hat revealing a compulsion to lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' rearranges the hat, and 'in' says the Arab goes inside the rearranged letters. 'Blimey!' and 'My!' are both mild exclamations of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythomania is a psychological term for an abnormal tendency to tell lies or exaggerate.

clue.text: Charge politician over stealing pounds

indicators.note: the politician stealing the money takes it inside himself
in a down clue, over means the whole thing is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of that political party
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An accusation that a politician has been pocketing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LIB round to BIL, and 'stealing' takes L inside it. The blog reverses after inserting; the result is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a statement of the charge owed for goods or services.

clue.text: Meat Buccaneer's unfortunately brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from the bottom upwards, so reversed

parts.note: Buccaneer is the setter, so 'Buccaneer's' becomes I'm, the setter speaking
alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: The setter admits to unluckily vomiting some meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Buccaneer, so 'Buccaneer's' stands for I'M; with ALAS it gives IMALAS, which 'brought up' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced sausage, a kind of preserved meat.

clue.text: Christmas plant left out on reportedly feeble period before Easter

indicators.note: left out means that letter is omitted from the plant

parts.note: holly is the evergreen used in Christmas decorations

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is said aloud, so a weak-sounding word is spelt differently

parts.note: feeble means weak

explanation.surface: A Christmas plant left lying on a feeble stretch before Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops an L from HOLLY to give HOLY; 'reportedly' turns WEAK into WEEK, which is said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Week is the Christian name for the seven days ending in Easter Sunday.

clue.text: Worker, extremely lowly, follows the first man unwaveringly

indicators.note: follows puts the worker and its partner after the first man

parts.note: Adam was the first man in the Bible
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: extremely means take only the extremes, the outer letters

explanation.surface: A humble labourer resolutely follows Adam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives LY, the ends of 'lowly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantly means in a firm, unyielding way, never wavering from a position.

clue.text: Princess on stage with house in a state

parts.note: Princess Ida is the title character of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta

explanation.surface: A theatrical princess with a home somewhere in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty US states, in the north-west.

clue.text: Source of material for writer one knew changing lines

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the word knew are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines

explanation.surface: A writer someone knew who kept changing lines, looking for material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' makes NKWE from KNEW.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkwell holds the ink a pen-and-ink writer dips into, so the material comes from it.

clue.text: 6's partner 18 beside a track

parts.note: 18-across is BEN, a Scottish word for a mountain, so a hill
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A partner sitting by a track, cross-referenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BILL; 'ben' is a mountain in Scotland, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillary Clinton is the wife of former US President Bill Clinton.

clue.text: 6's partner briefly fashionable

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: cool means fashionable

explanation.surface: A partner who is, for a moment, in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BILL: to 'bill and coo' is to kiss and murmur like doves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'bill and coo' pairs the two words, so coo partners bill in that idiom.

clue.text: Charlie remains with Greek character covered in hair, a supplier of 2s

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: the Greek letter is covered in hair, sitting inside it

parts.note: a mane is a head of long hair
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie's ashes and a hairy Greek character, supplying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 is BANKNOTE, so the definition is something that dispenses banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: An automated teller dispenses paper money, which is what a banknote is.

clue.text: Keeps down 6 for IT journalist just halved at first

indicators.note: for here means standing in place of: the IT Bill comes in after the journalist pieces

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor, a newspaper journalist

indicators.note: halved at first means only the opening half of the word just is kept

parts.note: 6 is BILL, and the Bill famous in IT is Bill Gates

explanation.surface: An IT man stands in for a journalist, who is just halved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' gives JU, the first half of 'just'.
explanation.definitionFit: To subjugate a people is to bring them under control, keeping them down.

clue.text: Concerning appearance of mosaic Celt composed

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The look of a mosaic that a Celt put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetical is a variant of cosmetic, relating to outward looks rather than substance.

clue.text: English composer returned, one with a 6

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: An English composer comes back with an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BILL, here a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A grebe is a diving water bird, and every bird has a bill.

clue.text: Frenchman in the 6 — male, say, nearly seizing gun?

indicators.note: the shortened word seizing the gun holds it inside
nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: male is an example of a gender
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A Frenchman in a bill, maybe a male nearly grabbing a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' gives GENDE; 'seizing' takes ARM inside it. 'The Bill' is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer, and the Old Bill is slang for the police.

clue.text: 6's partner in capital city deposing king

indicators.note: deposing the king removes him from the city's name

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A partner in a capital where the king is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and Ben were the Flowerpot Men of a classic British children's TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben is Bill's companion in the BBC puppet series Bill and Ben.

clue.text: One with large 6 goes off westward, heading for Kansas

indicators.note: in an across clue, westward means read right to left, backwards

parts.note: food that goes off rots

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of Kansas

explanation.surface: Someone with a big bill leaves for the west, making for Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BILL, a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The stork is a long-legged wading bird known for its long, heavy bill.

clue.text: Rock used for sharpening — loosen it foolishly

indicators.note: doing something foolishly is doing it wrongly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Warning against loosening a whetstone carelessly.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilstone is a fine-grained whetstone lubricated with oil for honing blades.

clue.text: Nothing unlike 7?

definitions.meaning: British slang for nothing at all
7 is SALAMI, a sausage, so something unlike it is the answer

explanation.surface: Nothing at all resembles the cured meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means absolutely nothing; read literally it describes anything that isn't a sausage, unlike salami.

clue.text: Old 6 — what 6 is in this puzzle, given time

parts.note: BILL is the theme of this puzzle

explanation.surface: The setter points out that Bill is the theme, with time added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police; the Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: London's police force is the Metropolitan Police, and police in Britain are nicknamed the Old Bill.

clue.text: The French women showing what 6 may become

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: French women demonstrate how a bill may turn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary bill becomes an Act, a statute, once passed.

clue.text: Gastropod to lead deer around

parts.note: to win is to come out in the lead

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the deer is read backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: A snail is meant to lead a deer in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A winkle is a small edible sea snail, and snails are gastropods.

clue.text: Live with Heather in the country

parts.note: 'I am' means I live or exist, so live gives AM
Erica is the botanical genus of heather

explanation.surface: Living with a woman named Heather out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: America, the United States, is a country.

clue.text: Couple gripped by excitement

indicators.note: gripped by means the answer is held inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Two people seized with excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is informal for a romantic couple, as in 'they're an item'.

clue.text: Criminal admits dressing 6 in 25

indicators.note: the criminal admits, lets in, the dressing so it goes inside

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
lint is a fabric used as a wound dressing

explanation.surface: A crook confessing to wearing a bandage.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is BILL and 25 AMERICA: the Bill of note in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton was the 42nd President of the United States.

clue.text: Conservative struck 6

parts.note: struck means hit

explanation.surface: A Tory hit a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a note of money owed, such as a restaurant bill.

clue.text: Start of mantra you once repeated is rubbish!

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of mantra is taken

parts.note: repeated stands for the piece beside it said again: the old word for you a second time
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A mantra once chanted over and over is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' gives the archaic YE a second time, so the pieces read M, YE, YE.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is a dated exclamation of disbelief, like saying 'nonsense!'.

clue.text: Roman deity in a pile, curiously, of seabed creatures

indicators.note: the deity goes in the shuffled letters
curiously means oddly arranged, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: a faun is a Roman rural deity, half man half goat

explanation.surface: A Roman god found in a heap, oddly among seabed animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' turns A PILE into EPIAL, and 'in' puts FAUN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Epifaunal describes epifauna, animals living on the surface of the sea floor.
